newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast steady as buyers flee to sidelines.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast steady as buyers flee to sidelines.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline and diesel prices ended the day unchanged on Monday as buyers fled to the sidelines in the midst of the rally in NYMEX futures prices, traders said.
The run-up in front-month heating oil and gasoline futures prompted sellers to push up ask prices in Los Angeles and San Francisco, but buyers refused to go along for the ride.
"There's not much of anything going on," one trader said. "The buyers didn't agree with the run-up."
Recent heavy rains and snowstorms in the Pacific Northwest also have dampened agricultural demand as farmers wait for floodwaters to recede and fields to dry out, traders said.
CARB gasoline was talked 80/81.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles for third cycle January deliveries, with February deliveries talked one cent higher.
Regular unleaded was talked 78/79 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, with premium steady at 6 cents higher, traders said.
Jet fuel was heard done 86.50 cents a gallon for a third-cycle delivery earlier in the day, one trader said.
